title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' axiomatics, an attempt to found a 'tame topology' (topologie modérée, as in Esquisse §5) on a few order-theoretic relations between 'figures'.

The objects are:
- M: a class of basic pieces or 'multiplicités'.
- 𝔉: figures (finite or locally finite assemblies of pieces).
- ≤: inclusion-type order.
- ≪: 'raffinement' or sub-figure relation. On the page itself only the restrictions F_i ≪ F appear explicitly.
- ‖: disjointness. ≍ / ≭ is a compatibility or non-overlap relation; its exact meaning is not fixed on this page.
- Omb(X) = {Z ∈ M : Z ≪ X}: the 'shadow' of X. The next page makes this explicit.
- X_L: restriction or trace of X on L.

1) Diagram. It relates Omb F and Omb G to Omb(F) ∩ Omb(G), which maps to Omb(L), where L = F.G is the 'product'/intersection. The intended content: any Z with Z ≪ F and Z ≪ G satisfies Z ≪ L. So the common shadow is controlled by the shadow of the Inf-like L. This is the key step of the compatibility criteria At pol / Prop. on p.16. There, F ≭ G follows if:
- (i) for X in F̃, Y in G̃ minorized in M, X ∩ Y ∈ M (Inf condition);
- (ii) refinements X ≪ F, Y ≪ G with empty trace on L are disjoint.

2) AtSpéc. A compatibility criterion for 'special' objects (the object word is uncertain). It is At pol with the Inf condition (L = ∅ or L ∈ M) removed. The corresponding Propositions are the same as the previous ones, with the Inf hypothesis (i) dropped.

3) NB, a chain of implications between axioms:
- AtD + AtSpéc ⇒ AtC ⇒ AtD ⇒ AtD₀.
- AtD + At pol ⇒ AtC for locally finite objects.
AtD is presumably the disjointness axiom: refinements of disjoint things stay disjoint, cf. the Cor. on p.16. AtC is presumably the general compatibility axiom. The margin says only a weakened AtD' is needed: one asserts X' ‖ Y' only for X', Y' with empty trace on L. AtD' still implies AtD₀.

4) At fil (criterion of filtered Sups). Let F ∈ 𝔉 and let (F_i) be a family of refinements F_i ≪ F, filtered increasing for ≤. Suppose it is 'locally finite in F': for every x in the underlying F̄, the restrictions F_i|X are eventually stationary. Then Sup F_i exists in (𝔉, ≤). The margin asks whether one should instead require i ≤ j ⇒ F_i ≪ F_j and take the Sup for ≪; this becomes Corollary 2 on p.18.

5) Corollary 1 (assuming AtC). Gluing of refinements when F = Sup F_i. It comes in two versions: gluing over sub-figures of F, or over strata. This is a descent/sheaf-type statement for refinements of stratified figures.

Purpose: to build, from axioms on (M, ≤, ≪, ‖), a calculus of stratified figures that has Infs, compatible pairs, locally finite Sups and gluing. In other words, the order-theoretic skeleton of a tame-topology theory.
errors: Diagram: if the arrows are read as inclusions, the arrows Omb F → Omb F ∩ Omb G point the wrong way; the intersection includes into each shadow. More likely the diagram schematizes 'take the intersection, then compare with Omb(L)', not maps.
If L is a genuine Inf for ≪-type relations, one expects Omb(F) ∩ Omb(G) = Omb(L), not just a one-way map. The page does not say which direction is claimed, or under which axiom.
At fil: the local finiteness condition is written with a point x ∈ F̄ but restrictions F_i|X with capital X. Whether the stationarity is pointwise or per piece X of a neighbourhood is ambiguous.
The NB implication chain is asserted without proof. AtC ⇒ AtD ⇒ AtD₀ is plausible from the definitions. AtD + AtSpéc ⇒ AtC is not argued here.

ideas.what: Shadow Omb(X) of a figure (set of pieces refining it), and the comparison of common shadow with the shadow of the intersection L = F.G
ideas.modern_name: down-set / principal ideal in a poset; meet-semilattice condition

ideas.what: Compatibility criteria At pol / AtSpéc: whether the Inf condition can be dropped for 'special' objects
ideas.modern_name: compatibility/consistency of stratifications; existence of common refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather (stratifications), o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.)

ideas.what: Hierarchy of axioms AtD₀ ⇐ AtD ⇐ AtC ⇐ AtD + AtSpéc, and the weakened AtD'
At fil: existence of Sup of a filtered, locally finite (stationary) family of refinements
ideas.modern_name: locally finite unions/colimits of stratifications; locally finite families in o-minimal/subanalytic geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory and o-minimality

ideas.what: Corollary 1: gluing of refinements along sub-figures or along strata
ideas.modern_name: sheaf/descent property of refinements (stratifications form a stack-like object)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in stratified homotopy theory; constructible sheaves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only announces tame topology in general terms

missed.claim: An order-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology was being built: primitive relations ≤, ≪ (refinement), ‖ (disjointness), shadows Omb, and a graded hierarchy of compatibility axioms. It was meant to yield Infs, filtered locally finite Sups and gluing of refinements. The program was not completed, and no comparable axiomatic framework exists in the o-minimal or stratification literature.
missed.quote: NB AtD + AtSpéc ⇒ AtC ⇒ AtD ⇒ AtD₀ ... At fil (Critère des Sup filtrants) ... Alors Sup F_i existe dans 𝔉,≤
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Stratified homotopy theory (exit-paths, Lurie/Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine) works with categories of stratifications and refinements. A synthetic, poset-level axiomatics of refinement, disjointness and gluing could give a model-independent foundation that is currently missing.

missed.claim: There is an explicit open choice between taking filtered Sups for ≤ and for ≪ (margin). It is pursued as Corollary 2 on p.18, but the comparison is never settled.
missed.quote: Ou vaudrait-il mieux supposer (i≤j ⇒ F_i ≪ F_j)? ... (et prendre Sup pour ≪ ??)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to whether categories of stratifications admit filtered colimits along refinement maps, a technical point in stratified ∞-category theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A working page of a private axiomatic program. The individual statements (meets of shadows, locally finite Sups, gluing of refinements) are natural analogues of known facts about stratifications. The novelty lies only in the overall unpublished axiomatic framework, not in any striking result on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'la condition de C fini (L=∅ ou L∈M)' should probably read 'la condition de Inf (L=∅ ou L∈M)', matching p.16, where this condition means that {X,Y} has an Inf.
'en supprimant (ii)' likely reads 'en supprimant (i)' in the image. (i) is the Inf condition that AtSpéc removes.
'chaînes[?] dits spéciaux' is uncertain. 'dits' (masculine) suggests a masculine noun, possibly 'couples' or 'polyidéaux', rather than 'chaînes'.
The second implication line ends with an implied '⇒ AtC (loc. finis)': the arrow points to AtC with the annotation 'loc. finis' beneath.
'(ou ≤)' after F ∈ 𝔉 appears to be a crossed-out/inserted '(ou ≪)' or '(pour ≤)' — uncertain.
